subject: DPA annex: emergency export exception & temporary pseudonymization plan
messages:
From: J. Patel <j.patel@acmecare.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: AcmeCare Legal <legal@acmecare.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: emergency export exception + how we'll pseudonymize

Hi Diego,

We're responding to an incident that requires a time-limited export of a small set of customer PII from AcmeCare's EU tenant to an incident response partner in the US (DataTransit Ltd). Our legal team is preparing a DPA annex to permit this exception, and they asked for Redwood to confirm the operational controls you can apply during the export window.

Specifically we need:
- A short written plan for how Redwood will pseudonymize or redact direct identifiers prior to transfer (or confirm you cannot).
- Retention/auto-deletion guarantees for the exported subset (we expect <72 hours retention on the partner side).
- KMS and key custody facts (can keys be customer-held?; audit evidence).
- Any subprocessors involved in moving data off-platform for emergency cases.

Can you provide a short plan today so the AcmeCare legal team can include it in the annex? We attached AcmeCare's proposed annex template.

Thanks,
J. Patel
Counsel, AcmeCare
[Attachment: acmecare_dpa_annex_draft.docx (docx)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: J. Patel <j.patel@acmecare.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: emergency export exception + how we'll pseudonymize

Hi J.,

Thanks for the flag — we can support this but need to align on steps and a short checklist for the annex. High-level answers up front:

- Pseudonymization: Redwood can run a deterministic tokenization pass to remove direct identifiers (names, emails, national IDs) and replace them with reversible tokens tied to a temporary key. Reversibility will be restricted to the incident-response scope and access is time-limited.
- Retention: We can restrict the exported artifacts to a 72-hour retention policy on DataTransit; we will include a contractual requirement and automated deletion proof (log entry).
- Keys: We can issue a one-time wrapping key from your KMS (customer-managed if you prefer) which will be used to encrypt the export bundle. If customer KMS is not available, Redwood will use our export KM (with HSM-backed audit).
- Subprocessors: DataTransit Ltd will act as the incident response vendor. No other subprocessors will be involved in the transfer.

I attached a short operational checklist and a starter language block for the annex. Can Neha and Marcus confirm the logging/evidence language?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dpa_export_exception_template_v1.pdf (pdf); Attachment: pseudonymization-step-by-step.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, J. Patel <j.patel@acmecare.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: emergency export exception + how we'll pseudonymize

Diego — quick clarifications and proposed evidence text below.

Clarifications:
- Tokenization mode: we'll use irreversible hashing for identifiers that are not required for incident triage (e.g., marketing metadata). For items that the IR team needs to re-link (device IDs, session tokens), we will use reversible tokens encrypted with the one-time wrapping key.
- Audit evidence: export job will generate a signed manifest (SHA256) and an export log entry (timestamp, operator id, key id). We can share the manifest and log excerpt to AcmeCare Legal as part of the annex.
- Access controls: only two named Redwood operators + DataTransit SOC engineer will have access to the unencrypted export key; access is scoped and time-bound.

Proposed annex language (short):
"Redwood will perform a pre-export pseudonymization pass that replaces direct identifiers with tokens. For re-linkable tokens, exports will be encrypted using a one-time wrapping key supplied by (or escrowed with) the customer. Redwood will provide a signed export manifest and an audit log excerpt evidencing deletion after 72 hours."

I can add the manifest sample to the Drive doc. Marcus, can you confirm the operator role names and the deletion proof format?

—Neha
Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, J. Patel <j.patel@acmecare.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: emergency export exception + how we'll pseudonymize

Neha/Diego — confirmed. Operational bullets I will add to the annex:
- Export job flow: 1) scope selection by legal/CS (CSV of IDs), 2) pre-export tokenization job (hash or reversible token), 3) bundle creation and encryption with one-time key, 4) transfer via TLS to DataTransit, 5) automated deletion job scheduled at T+72h, 6) signed deletion log generated and shared.
- Operator names: Marcus Lin (privacy eng operator), Neha Kapoor (privacy eng reviewer).
- Deletion proof format: signed manifest (SHA256) + deletion log entry with timestamp and operator ID; we can provide both as PDF excerpts.
